answer: Seats are allotments, not keys: each member holds one numbered bed in a shared garden and must return, each season, a weighed harvest of the cultivar it withdrew, receipted by a miller who stamps the bed number. Mass balance polices it: one bed yields one sack, and that number is punched through the tag so no sack counts twice. A steward then walks the ridge above the plots at unpublished hours, checking tags face living plants, not painted boards: a wander no grower can schedule. A thousand puppets need a thousand beds, sacks and visits. Cost scales with identities; harvest does not.
